Check a project against the house layout

Source: R/check_project.R
check_project.Rd

check_project() checks a project folder against the rules of its file pbn.yml and prints one line per finding. In a non-interactive R session it quits with status 1 when any rule fails.

Usage

check_project(path = ".")

Arguments

path

The project folder. It MUST hold the file pbn.yml.

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of the findings with the columns rule, status, path and detail.

Details

The first line names the rule set of pbn.yml, and counts its changes and its allowed paths. A rule with no finding prints one PASS line, and a rule that is off prints one OFF line. Each finding prints one line: PASS|WARN|FAIL <rule> <detail>. The detail of a WARN or a FAIL ends with Fix: and the change that removes the finding. A count line comes last.

Every rule reads one list of files and their folders:

  • When path is the top folder of a git repository, the list is the output of git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard. These are the tracked files, and the untracked files that git does not ignore.

  • Otherwise, the list is every file and folder on disk.

Both lists leave out .DS_Store, .Rhistory, .RData, the Word lock files ~$*, and everything in .git/ or .Rproj.user/.

The rules, with their level in the set house_2026_11_27, are below. The set house_2026_11_26 has the same rules at the same levels, without display_numbering. The set house_2026_11_25 also does not have built_reads_source, manual_has_supplement, manual_si_has_main, guidelines_valid and guidelines_covered. The set house_2026_11_20 also does not have no_plot_title, no_plot_subtitle and no_plot_caption. The set house_2026_11_19 also does not have built_reads_own_version, built_has_run and manual_not_ahead. The set house_2026_11_17 also does not have frozen_versions_unchanged, readme_and_changelog, changelog_with_code, comment_share, no_cross_version_reads and no_escape_hatches. A rule that the set of the project does not have prints no line.

  • lower_case_names (FAIL): a file or folder name has a capital letter. Everything under background/ is not checked. These are exempt: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE, DESCRIPTION, a top-level dotfile, a top-level *.Rproj file, file extensions, and the initials in manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx and manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>_<suffix>.docx, and in the drafts of an agent with the same names in manuscript/draft/.

  • run_script_initialises (FAIL): a vNN_run.R at the top level has no call pbn::initialize_project() whose version argument is the string "vNN". A call with an argument that initialize_project() does not have does not count, and the detail names that argument.

  • version_items_complete (FAIL): a vNN_run.R has no vNN_functions/, or the reverse.

  • frozen_versions_unchanged (FAIL): one of these is true:

    • a version older than the newest has no vNN_frozen.md5 of freeze_version(). A version is a vNN_run.R or a vNN_functions/ at the top level, and the newest is the one with the largest NN. So a deleted vNN_frozen.md5 of an older version fails. The newest version needs none. The fix names the call pbn::freeze_version("vNN").

    • a file of a version changed, came or went after freeze_version() wrote its vNN_frozen.md5. The files are vNN_run.R and each file under vNN_functions/, as freeze_version() lists them from the disk. The detail names the file, with changed, added or removed. A .R file whose line ends change between LF and CR LF, and nothing else, does not count as changed. A change of the line ends of any other file counts, see freeze_version().

    • a line of vNN_frozen.md5 is not <md5> <path>.

  • readme_and_changelog (FAIL): README.md or CHANGELOG.md is not at the top level, or CHANGELOG.md has no section for a version. A section is a line that starts with ## vNN, with a space or nothing after it, for example ## v01 or ## v01 (2026-11-19). A version is a vNN_run.R or a vNN_functions/ at the top level. From the set house_2026_11_20, a version is also the vNN of a file manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx with a name that manual_manuscript_names passes. README.md says what the project is, how to run it and why its code is as it is. CHANGELOG.md says what changed in each version. The detail is README.md: missing, CHANGELOG.md: missing or CHANGELOG.md: no section "## vNN".

  • changelog_with_code (WARN): in a git repository, a vNN_run.R or a file under vNN_functions/ differs from the last commit, and CHANGELOG.md does not. A change is staged or not staged, or the file is untracked and git does not ignore it. A deleted file counts too. In a repository without a commit, each staged file is a change. The rule reads the project folder path only, also when it is a folder inside a repository. When git is not installed or path is not in a git repository, the rule has nothing to compare. It then prints one PASS line that says so. The detail is <file>: changed since the last commit, and CHANGELOG.md did not change.

  • results_contract (FAIL): a vNN_results/<scenario>/results.qs2 or a vNN_results/<scenario>/sim_NNNN/results.qs2 of pbn 2026.11.22 fails check_results(), or a results.qs2 is directly in vNN_results/.

    The rule also reads each vNN_results/<scenario>/sims_gitexclude/sim_NNNN.qs2 on the disk, also when git ignores it, and fails a file that fails check_results(). A clone of the repository has none, and the rule then needs none.

    The rule also reads each results_gitexclude.qs2 beside a results.qs2, and each sim_NNNN_gitexclude.qs2 beside a sim_NNNN.qs2, also when git ignores it. It fails when the file does not hold exactly the analysis kinds that the manifest of the results file puts there. check_results() does not check it.

  • gitexclude_not_tracked (FAIL): git tracks a path with gitexclude in its name, from git ls-files in path. Such a path holds data for each person. When git is not installed or path is not in a git repository, the rule has nothing to check. It then prints one PASS line that says so.

  • scenario_checks (FAIL): a vNN_results/<scenario>/check.csv has a value of pass that is not TRUE, holds no assertion, or has no column pass that R can read. save_results() writes these files.

  • manual_manuscript_names (FAIL): a file in manuscript/manual/ does not match ^v[0-9]{2}_[A-Z]{2,4}[0-9]?(_[a-z0-9]+)?\.docx$. The suffix is one word of lower-case letters and digits, for a second file of the same version, such as the supporting information v02_AB_si.docx.

  • manuscript_reads_real (FAIL): an .R, .qmd or .Rmd file in manuscript/built/ calls read_results() or pbn::read_results() with a scenario argument that is not the string "real". A call without scenario passes. In .qmd and .Rmd files, the rule reads the R chunks that knitr::purl() extracts and the inline R code.

  • built_reads_own_version (FAIL): an .R, .qmd or .Rmd file in manuscript/built/vNN/ calls read_results() or pbn::read_results() with a version argument that is not the string "vNN". A variable and a call without version fail too. The rule reads the code as manuscript_reads_real does, and it fails a file that R cannot parse. It does not read a file in manuscript/built/ outside a folder vNN/, or a file of another language, such as .py. The detail lists each call that fails. From the set house_2026_11_26, the rule also reads each txt() call and each read_blocks() call.

  • built_reads_source (FAIL): a file in manuscript/built/vNN/ does not read the numbers of its source. A version is one-file when its vNN_run.R gives one_file_home in a top-level call pbn::initialize_project(). pbn parses the run script and runs nothing. In a one-file version, a file fails without a read_blocks() or txt() call, and on a read_results() call. Each file there also fails while vNN_results/real/blocks.qs2 does not exist, or has the attribute pbn_fake of import_blocks(), because the numbers are then fake. In another version, a file fails on a read_blocks() call. The rule reads the code as manuscript_reads_real does. It does not read a file outside a folder vNN/.

  • built_has_run (FAIL): a folder manuscript/built/vNN/ has no vNN_run.R at the top level. In a git repository, an empty folder is not in the list of files, so the rule does not see it. The detail is manuscript/built/vNN: there is no vNN_run.R.

  • manual_not_ahead (FAIL): a file manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx has NN at or above MM, the largest version of a vMM_run.R. The run scripts and the manuscripts share one version counter. So a hand edit of version vMM is v(MM+1)_<INITIALS>.docx, and the next run version is v(MM+2). The detail is manual vNN is ahead of the newest run vMM: freeze vMM and start vPP with pbn::new_version("vMM", to = "vPP"), with PP = NN + 1. The rule does not read a name that manual_manuscript_names fails. Without a vNN_run.R, the rule has nothing to compare. It then prints one PASS line that says so.

  • manual_has_supplement (FAIL): a main file manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx has no supplement manuscript/manual/vMM_<INITIALS>_si.docx with MM at or below NN. The initials of the supplement MAY differ. The supplement suffix is exactly si, so a file with another suffix is neither a main file nor a supplement. The rule reads manuscript/manual/ only, so a draft in manuscript/draft/ does not count. A project without a supplement turns the rule off with rules: manual_has_supplement: off in pbn.yml.

  • manual_si_has_main (FAIL): a supplement manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>_si.docx has no main file manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx with the same version and the same initials. The detail names the main file to add.

  • fake_data_names (FAIL): a file in a folder output_fake_data/ has a name without the prefix fake_data_, or a file with the prefix is in another folder. make_outputs() writes these folders.

  • no_local_copy_of_pbn_function (FAIL): a top-level assignment in a vNN_functions/*.R file defines a function with the name of a pbn export. The one exception is get_data: a project MAY name its data function get_data(scenario, sim), and a run script calls the export as pbn::get_data(). The set house_2026_11_17 does not know the exports create_project, freeze_version, new_version and verify, so a local function with such a name passes there.

  • loc_per_file (FAIL): an .R file has more than limit code lines, as counted by org::loc_per_file(). The house limit is 1000. The rule reads each .R file of the project but vNN_one_file.R.

  • cyclomatic_complexity (FAIL): a function scores above limit in cyclocomp::cyclocomp(). The house limit is 15, the limit of the lint gate of the house packages. The rule reads the .R files of loc_per_file. It scores each function that a top-level assignment defines, and each function in a list() of a top-level assignment, as <list>$<name>. A function inside a function counts toward the outer function. Top-level code that is not a function gets no score. The rule parses each file and runs no code of it. It skips a file that R cannot parse, which loc_per_file fails. The detail gives the file, the function and its score. A path under allow allows each function of one file.

  • comment_share (WARN): in vNN_run.R or an .R file at the top of vNN_functions/, the share of comment lines is more than limit. The share is the comment lines divided by the lines that are not blank. The house limit is 0.25, so a file of 20 such lines MAY have 5 comment lines. The parse data decides what is a comment, so a # in a string does not count. A line with code and a comment after it is a comment line. A section marker is not a comment line. A section marker is a comment with text and then four or more = or - at its end, as in # PART 1 ====. The rule skips a file that R cannot parse. The detail is <file>: <n> of <m> lines that are not blank are comments, <share>, above the limit of <limit>. An explanation of why the code is as it is goes into README.md, and what changed goes into CHANGELOG.md.

  • no_environment_variables (FAIL): a run script or a file in a functions folder uses Sys.getenv or Sys.setenv.

  • no_cross_version_reads (FAIL): a string constant of vNN_run.R or of an .R file at the top of vNN_functions/ names another version or the folder adhoc/. The rule splits each string at / and \. A string fails when one of its parts is one of these:

    • vMM, with MM other than NN, as in read_results("v01") in v02_run.R.

    • vMM_ and an item of the layout: run.R, functions, results, cache_gitexclude, test, check_functions.R, one_file.R or frozen.md5. An example is "../v01_functions/get_data.R".

    • adhoc, as in "adhoc/helpers.R".

    These pass:

    • the version of the file and its items, and a comment.

    • a column name such as "v01_age", and "v1" and "v100".

    • a part with more words, such as "an adhoc analysis of v01".

    • a string that paste0() or sprintf() builds. The rule misses it.

    A column or a level with the name v01 fails, so allow its file in pbn.yml. The rule skips a file that R cannot parse, and a string of more than 1000 bytes. The detail is <file>:<line>: "<the string, cut at 40 characters>" names vMM, or names adhoc/.

  • no_local_assign (FAIL): an .R file uses a construct of forbid at any depth. The house forbid holds all seven constructs: local(), assign(), delayedAssign(), assignInNamespace(), assignInMyNamespace(), <<- and ->>. Each of these creates or changes an object in a place other than the line where it stands. The rule reads the .R files of loc_per_file, parses each file and runs no code of it. A call with the prefix of its own package, base:: or utils::, counts. A call of the same name from another package passes. A variable or an argument named local or assign passes, and so do <-, ->, = and :=. The rule skips a file that R cannot parse. The detail gives the file, the line and the construct. A path under allow allows each finding of one file.

  • no_escape_hatches (WARN): vNN_run.R or an .R file at the top of vNN_functions/ calls suppressWarnings(), suppressMessages(), try(), tryCatch() or withCallingHandlers(), at any depth. Each of these can hide a warning or an error of the run. A call with the prefix base:: counts. A call of the same name from another package passes. So do a word in a comment or a string, and a variable or an argument named try. The rule skips a file that R cannot parse. The detail gives the file, the line and the call. A path under allow allows each finding of one file. Give the reason in a comment in pbn.yml.

  • no_absolute_paths (FAIL): a string constant of an .R file of loc_per_file is an absolute path, or a path starts from a string constant. The rule reads the strings from the parse data, so a comment does not count. The arguments of a call pbn::initialize_project() are exempt, because a project declares its paths there, also one_file_home and one_file_folders. A string is an absolute path when it starts with one of these:

    • /, a name of letters, digits, ., _ or - that starts with a letter or _, and / again, as in "/home/a/x.csv" or "/data/".

    • ~/ or ~\, the home folder.

    • a drive letter, : and / or \, as in "C:/x", "C:\\x" or "N:/durable/x".

    • \\ and a letter or a digit, the start of a UNC path such as "\\\\server\\share".

    These strings pass:

    • "/" and "~".

    • the regular expressions "^/", "/$" and "/.*$".

    • a URL such as "https://a.org/b".

    • the formats "%s/%s" and "%Y/%m/%d", and the fraction "1/2".

    • the formula "y ~ x", and "/month".

    • the relative paths "data/x.csv", "./x" and "../x". A path with .. leaves the project folder, and it passes too.

    • a path with one name and no second /, such as "/data", and a string of more than 1000 bytes. The rule misses these.

    The rule also fails a call of file.path(), base::file.path() or fs::path() whose first argument is a string constant, for example file.path("data", "x.csv") or file.path("/", "data"). A path that starts from a constant is absolute, or it depends on the working directory. A path to data starts from pbn::folder(). A path for output starts from the folder that pbn gives the function, such as dir of make_outputs(). A call whose first argument is a name or a call passes, for example file.path(dir, "fig2.png") or file.path(tempdir(), "x"). A path that paste0() or sprintf() builds stays outside the rule.

    The detail is <file>:<line>: "<the string, cut at 40 characters>", or <file>:<line>: file.path("<the first argument, cut at 40 characters>", ...). A path under allow allows each finding of one file.

  • no_plot_title (FAIL): an .R file of loc_per_file gives a figure a title. A figure has no title, no subtitle and no caption, because its legend belongs in the manuscript. The rule fails each of these:

    • a call ggtitle() with a value of its first argument label.

    • an argument title of labs().

    • an argument title of plot_annotation(), by name or as its first argument.

    • an assignment to <x>$labels$title.

    A call MAY have the prefix ggplot2:: for ggtitle() and labs(), and patchwork:: for plot_annotation(). A call of the same name from another package passes. R matches the arguments of a call as it does in a run: by name, by a part of a name and by position. These pass:

    • the value NULL, as in labs(title = NULL), which removes the title.

    • the other arguments, as in labs(x = "Age", colour = "Group", tag = "A") and plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A").

    • a theme element, as in theme(plot.title = element_text()).

    • an argument title or caption of another function, as in knitr::kable(d, caption = "x").

    • a call that R cannot match, as one with an argument that the function does not have, and a title that do.call() or a ... passes. The rule misses these.

    The rule parses each file and runs no code of it. It skips a file that R cannot parse. The detail is <file>:<line>: <call>(<argument> = ...), for example v01_functions/output.R:12: ggplot2::labs(title = ...), or <file>:<line>: <target> <- .... A path under allow allows each finding of one file.

  • no_plot_subtitle (FAIL): as no_plot_title, for a subtitle: the argument subtitle of ggtitle(), by name or as its second argument, the argument subtitle of labs() and of plot_annotation(), and an assignment to <x>$labels$subtitle.

  • no_plot_caption (FAIL): as no_plot_title, for a caption: the argument caption of labs() and of plot_annotation(), and an assignment to <x>$labels$caption.

  • blocks_list (FAIL): for each functions folder, one of these is true:

    • a file other than vNN_functions/blocks.R assigns blocks at its top level. pbn leaves blocks.R out of manifest$source_md5, so the blocks MUST be in that file.

    • more than one top-level assignment of blocks.R assigns it.

    • its value is not a call of list(), or the list is empty.

    • an element has no name, or a name comes twice.

    • an element is not a function, or the name of a function that a top-level assignment of the functions folder defines.

    • a top-level expression of blocks.R is not an assignment with <- or = of a name to function(...), or of blocks to list(...). Examples are library(x), options(...), set.seed(1), an if and fmt <- sprintf. Such code runs when pbn sources the folder, so it can change the results.

    • a name that blocks.R assigns at its top level, and another file of the folder assigns too. The detail names both places.

    • another file of the folder, or vNN_run.R, uses a name that blocks.R assigns at its top level. Examples are a helper fmt(), and CFG after CFG$labels <- ... in blocks.R. The run would then depend on a file outside source_md5. A name after $ or @ and the name of an argument do not count.

    The detail is <file>:<line>: <what>. A folder without blocks and without blocks.R passes. initialize_project() makes the same checks of blocks.R, and puts it back into manifest$source_md5 when one fails, also when this rule is warn or off.

    From the set house_2026_11_26, the rule also fails each of these:

    • an element of blocks that is not a call pbn::block(fn, format, items).

    • a format that is not one string, or that names no house formatter and no function of formatters.R.

    • an items that is not a literal c("<id>:<item>", ...) of strings.

    • a top-level expression of vNN_functions/formatters.R that does not assign a name to function(...).

    • a name of formatters.R that a file other than blocks.R uses or assigns.

    The rule does not run the blocks, so it does not see their raw values. save_results(), update_blocks(), show_blocks(), show_block() and txt() check each raw value as block() says.

  • real_results_are_fake (WARN): a file vNN_results/real/results.qs2 holds manifest$fake_real_data TRUE. Its run had fake_real_data = TRUE of initialize_project(), so its numbers are not those of the real data. It passes when no such file is in the list of files. In a git repository, a real results file that git ignores is not in the list, so the rule does not see it.

  • guidelines_valid (FAIL): a file guidelines/<x>.yml breaks the checklist schema below. Each such file gives one FAIL, and its detail names its first 3 problems and counts the rest. The rule reads each .yml file directly in guidelines/. It does not read a file in a folder under guidelines/, or a file with another extension, such as .yaml.

  • guidelines_covered (WARN): a result item of a valid file guidelines/<x>.yml has no block, or a block names an item that no valid file has. Each such item and each such tag gives one WARN. The rule reads the literal items of each block() in the blocks.R of the newest functions folder, without running code. A tag of a file that fails guidelines_valid gives no WARN. make_checklists() then checks the manuscript text against the formatted strings of the blocks.

  • display_numbering (FAIL): the numbered figures and tables of the outputs, of the manuscript and of its citations do not agree. The rule reads the output folders vNN_results/<scenario>/output/ and vNN_results/<scenario>/output_fake_data/ of the newest run version. It reads each name there without the prefix fake_data_. Each name MUST be one of these:

    • fig_N_<name> or fig_sN_<name>, a figure, with any extension. N is a whole number from 1, and s marks a supplementary figure.

    • tables.xlsx, with one sheet tab_N or tab_sN for each numbered table.

    • data_behind_figures.xlsx, with the plotted data in sheets fig_N_<name> or fig_sN_<name>. A figure MAY have more than one sheet.

    • fig_N_<name>_external.txt, fig_sN_<name>_external.txt, tab_N_<name>_external.txt or tab_sN_<name>_external.txt, an item that the output function does not make, such as a flow chart.

    • nonum_<name>, anything else.

    A sheet nonum_<name> passes in both workbooks. A file tab_N_<name> that does not end with _external.txt fails, because tables go in tables.xlsx. Each figure file other than an _external.txt item MUST have a sheet of its number in data_behind_figures.xlsx of its folder. Each sheet fig_N_ MUST have a figure file of its number there.

    The manuscript is the newest version NN of manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx, then its _si files, and the files manuscript/built/vNN/*.md. Without a manuscript, the rule checks the names only. A citation is "Figure 1", "Fig. 1", "Table 1", "Figure S1" or "Supplementary Figure 1", which is Figure S1. A range such as "Tables 1-3" cites each number of it. A list needs the plural word, and it follows the Oxford comma. It has two items, as in "Figures 1 and 2", or three or more that end in ", and", as in "Figures 1, 2, and 3". A range MAY be an item. A list such as "Figures 1, 2 and 3" fails, and its items still count as citations. A comma after one item ends the citation, so "Figures 1 and 2, 25 and 30 persons" cites Figures 1 and 2 only. The text of a tracked deletion and of the old place of moved text in a .docx file does not count. There are four series: the figures, the tables, the supplementary figures and the supplementary tables. In each series, the first citations MUST come in the order 1, 2, 3, with no gap. A paragraph that starts with "Figure 2." or "Table S1:" is a caption. So is "Figure 2." in Markdown emphasis, and "", the text of an image. The text MUST cite each captioned item outside its own caption.

    The numbered items of the outputs are the figure files, the sheets tab_ of tables.xlsx and the _external.txt items of vNN_results/real/output/. Without that folder, they are the items of the first output_fake_data/ folder of the version in name order, such as fake/output_fake_data/ of a one-file project. Each numbered item MUST be cited or captioned in the manuscript. Each item of the manuscript MUST be a numbered item of the outputs. The PASS line names the folder.

  • unknown_path (WARN): the house layout does not name a top-level file or folder. The layout names vNN_run.R, vNN_functions/, vNN_results/, vNN_cache_gitexclude/, vNN_test/, vNN_check_functions.R, vNN_one_file.R, check_project.R and pbn.yml, among others. From the set house_2026_11_19, it also names vNN_frozen.md5 of freeze_version(). From the set house_2026_11_26, it also names the folder guidelines/. A top-level dotfile and a top-level *.Rproj file are never unknown. The rule also reads the files directly in vNN_results/. There it names the run log run.md, its PDF run.pdf and its errors file run_errors_gitexclude.md, and no rule needs them. It reads no deeper, so it never warns on the folders output/ and output_fake_data/ that make_outputs() writes in vNN_results/<scenario>/, or on the folder sims_gitexclude/ that save_results() writes there.

A checklist file guidelines/<x>.yml holds one reporting guideline, in the checklist schema of the methods repository. Copy the file from there. guidelines_valid fails the file unless each of these is true:

  • The file is valid YAML, and a map.

  • It has no key other than id, title, version, source, citation, designs, design and items.

  • id and title are each one string. id has only the characters a-z, 0-9 and -, and no other file has the same id.

  • version, source and citation MAY be missing. Each one that is there is one string.

  • A key that is there has a value. version: with nothing after it, or citation: ~, fails. This holds for designs and design too, and for the designs of an entry.

  • designs MAY be missing. When it is there, it is a YAML sequence of strings, such as [cohort]. One string, such as designs: cohort, or a map fails. The same holds for the designs of an entry.

  • design MAY be missing. When it is there, it is one of designs.

  • items is a YAML sequence with at least one entry. A map fails.

  • Each entry has no key other than item, section, topic, kind, designs and text. Its item, section, topic, kind and text are each one string. Quote an item id such as "2", because YAML reads 2 as a number.

  • The kind of each entry is result, prose or author.

  • The designs of an entry MAY be missing, and the entry then belongs to each design of the file. When it is there, the file has designs, and each value is one of them.

  • An item id comes once per design, among the entries that design keeps. STROBE has three entries with the item id 15, one for each design, so it passes.

A project copy MAY add the key design, such as design: cohort. pbn then keeps the entries whose designs include it, and the entries without designs.

The R parser, not a regular expression, finds the calls, the assignments and the symbols.

vNN_one_file.R at the top level is the file of to_one_file(). It holds the paths of a server by design, and pbn writes it. So loc_per_file, cyclomatic_complexity, no_local_assign, no_absolute_paths, no_plot_title, no_plot_subtitle and no_plot_caption do not read it, and no rule takes it for a run script. Put it in git: it is what ran on the server.

The file pbn.yml

Each project MUST have the file pbn.yml in its top folder path. pbn reads no other file. A file pbn.yaml stops check_project() with the advice to rename it. The smallest pbn.yml is one line:

extends: house_2026_11_25

The key extends names a house rule set. A set is a dated file in the folder rules/ of pbn, and pbn never changes a set after its release. A change to the house rules is a new set with a new date. pbn never chooses a set for a project. So a new version of pbn does not change the rules of a project. To read the set, run readLines(system.file("rules", "house_2026_11_25.yml", package = "pbn")).

The set gives each rule one of three levels:

  • fail: a finding is FAIL, and check_project.R ends with status 1.

  • warn: a finding is WARN.

  • off: the rule does not run, and its one line is OFF.

The parameters of the rules are limit of loc_per_file, limit of cyclomatic_complexity, limit of comment_share and forbid of no_local_assign. The list of the rules above gives their house values.

The key rules MAY change the level of a rule, a parameter, or both. A change merges into the entry of the set. So cyclomatic_complexity: {limit: 25} keeps the level fail. The short form lower_case_names: warn changes the level only. forbid MAY list fewer constructs than the house set.

The key allow MAY list paths for each rule, relative to path. A path allows the findings with that path and the findings of each path under it. So the folder adhoc allows adhoc/Notes.txt and adhoc/Old/Data.csv, but not adhoc2/x.R. A final / changes nothing: adhoc and adhoc/ are the same entry. pbn does not look on the disk for a file or a folder of that name. An allowed finding is WARN, with (allowed) before its fix. A path that matches no finding is a WARN of the rule allow.

Three rules are locked: results_contract, gitexclude_not_tracked and fake_data_names. The first two keep data for each person out of git. The third keeps the output of fake data apart from the output of real data. pbn.yml cannot set a locked rule to warn or off, and cannot allow a path for it. It cannot name a rule of check_results() either.

The key ignore MAY list folders at the top level, such as archive/, that no rule reads: their files give no finding, not even a WARN. Use it for old work that nothing runs. A final / changes nothing. An entry MUST be one folder at the top level that the house layout of the set does not name, so it cannot be manuscript/, background/, adhoc/ or a folder of a version. From the set house_2026_11_26, it cannot be guidelines/ either. A folder that does not exist is no error. The locked rules still read an ignored folder, so a tracked file with gitexclude in its name fails there too. The first line of the report counts the ignored folders.

This pbn.yml changes two rules, allows three paths and ignores one folder:

extends: house_2026_11_25
rules:
  cyclomatic_complexity: {limit: 25}
  unknown_path: off
allow:
  lower_case_names: [adhoc/Old_notes.txt, adhoc/Drafts/]
  no_local_assign:
    - adhoc/explore.R
ignore: [archive/]

check_project() and initialize_project() stop before any rule runs on each of these, with a message that names the key:

  • there is no pbn.yml. The message gives the one line to write.

  • there is a file pbn.yaml, or a file pbn_allow.txt. For pbn_allow.txt, the message gives its lines as the YAML of the key allow.

  • pbn.yml is not valid YAML. This includes a key that is there twice and a tab. The message holds the message of the yaml package.

  • there is no key extends, or it names a set that pbn does not have.

  • a key other than extends, rules, allow and ignore.

  • a name that is not a rule. The message names the nearest rule.

  • a rule that the set of extends does not have. The message names the oldest set with it.

  • a parameter that the rule does not have.

  • a level other than fail, warn and off.

  • a limit that is not a whole number of 1 or more. For comment_share, a limit that is not a number from 0 to 1.

  • a construct in forbid that the rule does not know, or an empty forbid. To turn the rule off, set its level to off.

  • a value under allow that is not a path, for example off. YAML reads off, yes and no as booleans, so a path with such a name needs quotes.

  • a change or an allowed path of a locked rule.

  • an entry of ignore that is not one folder at the top level, is a name of the house layout, is there twice, or is a file.

See also

Other checks: freeze_version(), verify()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_check_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines("extends: house_2026_11_25", file.path(home, "pbn.yml"))
writeLines(
  'pbn::initialize_project(version = "v01", home = ".", folders = c(main = "x"))',
  file.path(home, "v01_run.R")
)
writeLines("# A fake project", file.path(home, "README.md"))
writeLines(c("# Changelog", "", "## v01"), file.path(home, "CHANGELOG.md"))
pbn::check_project(home)
#> Rules: house_2026_11_25, 0 overrides, 0 allowed paths (pbn.yml)
#> PASS  lower_case_names  no capital letter in a name
#> PASS  run_script_initialises  every vNN_run.R calls pbn::initialize_project() with its own version
#> PASS  version_items_complete  every vNN_run.R has a vNN_functions/, and the reverse
#> PASS  frozen_versions_unchanged  every version but the newest has a vNN_frozen.md5, and no file of a frozen version changed after pbn::freeze_version()
#> PASS  readme_and_changelog  README.md and CHANGELOG.md exist, and CHANGELOG.md has a section ## vNN for every version
#> PASS  changelog_with_code  the project is not a git repository, so nothing to compare
#> PASS  results_contract  every vNN_results/<scenario>/results.qs2 and each vNN_results/<scenario>/sims_gitexclude/sim_NNNN.qs2 on the disk passes check_results()
#> PASS  gitexclude_not_tracked  the project is not a git repository, so nothing to check
#> PASS  scenario_checks  every vNN_results/<scenario>/check.csv passes
#> PASS  manual_manuscript_names  every file in manuscript/manual/ is named vNN_<INITIALS>.docx or vNN_<INITIALS>_<suffix>.docx
#> PASS  manuscript_reads_real  manuscript/built/ reads only the real results
#> PASS  built_reads_own_version  every read_results() call in manuscript/built/vNN/ reads the version vNN
#> PASS  built_has_run  every folder manuscript/built/vNN/ has a vNN_run.R
#> PASS  manual_not_ahead  every manuscript/manual/vNN_<INITIALS>.docx is older than the newest run version
#> PASS  fake_data_names  every file in an output_fake_data/ folder, and no file elsewhere, has a name that starts with fake_data_
#> PASS  no_local_copy_of_pbn_function  no vNN_functions/ file defines a pbn export
#> PASS  loc_per_file  no .R file has more than 1000 code lines
#> PASS  cyclomatic_complexity  no function of an .R file has a cyclomatic complexity above 15
#> PASS  comment_share  no run script or .R file of a functions folder has more than 25% comment lines
#> PASS  no_environment_variables  no Sys.getenv or Sys.setenv in a run script or a functions folder
#> PASS  no_cross_version_reads  no string in a run script or a functions folder names another version or adhoc/
#> PASS  no_local_assign  no .R file calls local, assign, delayedAssign, assignInNamespace or assignInMyNamespace, or uses <<- or ->>
#> PASS  no_escape_hatches  no run script or functions folder calls suppressWarnings(), suppressMessages(), try(), tryCatch() or withCallingHandlers()
#> PASS  no_absolute_paths  no .R file has an absolute path or a file.path() from a string, outside the arguments of pbn::initialize_project()
#> PASS  no_plot_title  no .R file gives a figure a title
#> PASS  no_plot_subtitle  no .R file gives a figure a subtitle
#> PASS  no_plot_caption  no .R file gives a figure a caption
#> PASS  blocks_list  blocks, when a functions folder has it, is a list of named functions in vNN_functions/blocks.R, and no other code uses a name of that file
#> PASS  real_results_are_fake  no real results on the disk come from fake real data
#> PASS  unknown_path  the house layout names every top-level path
#> 30 PASS, 0 WARN, 0 FAIL, 0 OFF

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
